ideas.title: Shop-in-Shop Stock
ideas.summary: For small Shopify brands that keep a few products on unattended shelves inside cafés, gyms and salons: a QR code per shelf, phone checkout through the brand's own Shopify store, and stock tracked per shelf without paying for a Shopify location at each one.

public.summary: Lets shoppers buy from your unattended shelves in other people's shops by scanning a code, and tells you exactly what is left on each shelf.
public.problem: You have a small shelf of your products in a café, a gym and a salon, with nobody there to sell them. A shopper scans a code and pays on your web store, but you have no idea which shelf that sale came from or what is left on it. So you drive round guessing what to restock and settle up with each host from memory.
public.forWhom: Small brands that place their products on shelves inside other local businesses.
benefits: Shoppers pay on their own phone, no staff or till at the shelf
See what is left on every shelf at a glance
Get a restock list for your next round of visits
Spot missing stock early, shelf by shelf
Hand each host a clear commission statement

ideas.problemStatement: A brand with products on unattended shelves at many partner locations needs each sale paid on the shopper's phone and deducted from that shelf's stock. Shopify caps locations at 10 below Plus and 200 on Plus, the nearest QR-checkout app is priced per Shopify location, and the nearest stockist app expects the partner to enter sales by hand.
ideas.description: Each shelf gets a printed QR code that opens a page listing only what is in stock at that shelf; the shopper adds items and pays through the brand's normal Shopify checkout, with the shelf ID carried as a cart attribute. A small Shopify app reads paid orders by webhook, deducts the shelf's stock in its own ledger (outside Shopify's location model), and guards against double deduction and stale carts. The owner side handles warehouse-to-shelf transfers, route restock lists, stock counts with shrink reports, and per-host commission statements. Shopify keeps payments, receipts, refunds and tax.
ideas.targetCustomer: Owners of small Shopify brands (coffee roasters, candle and snack makers, skincare, local crafts) with 5 to 200 unattended product placements inside other businesses.
ideas.buyer: The brand owner, on a company card, as a monthly Shopify app charge.
ideas.whyNow: A Shopify merchant asked for exactly this on 2026-09-22 (412 views, 28 replies) and was told no single tool does it; PlaceStock (launched 2026-08-18) shows stockist tracking is being productized, but it relies on partners logging sales.
ideas.founderFit: A Shopify app with a stock ledger, a webhook consumer and a mobile page is a solo Supabase/React build; the hard parts (idempotent deduction, stale carts, reconciliation) are the systems problems he teaches. He has no retail network, so distribution leans on the Shopify App Store and community threads.

problemEvidence.author: ThomasOBG
problemEvidence.summary: Merchant wants QR phone checkout and per-location stock at 100 to 500 unattended shop-in-shop spots without POS hardware; replies say Shopify's location caps rule out native locations.

problemEvidence.author: shopoddbird
problemEvidence.summary: Adjacent: Shopify locations do not stop a pop-up from selling stock held at other locations (staffed case).

problemEvidence.author: PlaceStock (vendor)
problemEvidence.summary: Paid app for stock held at partner shops, $14.99 to $49.99 a month by partner count; 0 reviews, so price exists but buyers are unproven.

competitors.name: PlaceStock
competitors.gap: Partners enter sales themselves; no shopper QR checkout, so it does not fit unstaffed shelves.

competitors.name: Leav Scan & Go
competitors.gap: QR self-checkout tied to Shopify locations, so it hits the 10 or 200 location cap and per-shelf economics break.

competitors.name: Store Check-In
competitors.gap: Needs an iPad at each spot.

competitors.name: ConsignKit
competitors.gap: Built for shops selling other people's goods (inbound consignment), not brands placing stock outward.

competitors.name: TallyTill
competitors.gap: Honor-mode till with multi-location, but per-location stock with Shopify checkout is unconfirmed; Shopify import only.

keyFeatures: One QR code per shelf showing only that shelf's stock
Checkout through the brand's own Shopify store with the shelf ID on the order
Per-shelf stock ledger outside Shopify locations, with idempotent deduction
Route restock lists and stock counts with shrink reports
Monthly commission statement per host business

features: Shelf storefront page with cart attribute
Order webhook deduction with double-delivery guard
mvpScope.buildEstimate: 3 to 4 weeks, plus Shopify app review

ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind, Supabase (Postgres ledger, auth, edge functions for webhooks), Shopify Admin API and Storefront cart API; no LLM at runtime.

pricing.model: Shopify app subscription by number of shelves
pricing.rationale: In line with PlaceStock's $14.99 to $49.99 tiers and far below Leav's $495 unlimited tier; the requester budgets under $150 a month in sales per spot, so per-shelf cost must stay pennies.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate: 60 brands x $30/month average = $1,800 MRR, assuming the App Store and direct outreach to brands with stockist pages convert; unvalidated.
ideas.distribution: Reply in thread 686270 and newer pop-up or multi-location threads; Shopify App Store keywords (unattended, honesty shelf, stockists, consignment); direct outreach to small roasters, candle and snack brands whose stockist pages list cafés and gyms.

validationTest.method: Build a no-code prototype (one QR page per shelf linking to a Shopify cart with a shelf attribute, plus a spreadsheet ledger fed by order export) and offer it to ThomasOBG and 10 brands found through stockist pages.
validationTest.successCriteria: 3 brands run it on at least 5 shelves for a month and 2 agree to pay $19/month.

ideas.moat: Thin: per-shelf history and host statements create switching cost, but PlaceStock could add QR checkout cheaply.
compliance: Payments, PCI and receipts stay in Shopify checkout.
Sales tax should follow the shelf's address for in-person sales; tag each order with it and leave the tax decision to the merchant.
Host commissions may need 1099 reporting in the US (unverified).
Exclude age-restricted goods.
Shopify App Store GDPR webhooks and privacy policy.

risks.risk: Only one buyer was found and he was already talking to a provider by 2026-10-12.
risks.mitigation: The validation test must find 3 more brands before any build.

risks.risk: Theft and shrink at unattended shelves become a support burden.
risks.mitigation: Ship shrink reports and per-shelf counts; leave loss policy to the brand and the host.

risks.risk: Stale carts or duplicate webhooks deduct the wrong shelf.
risks.mitigation: Expire shelf carts quickly and make deduction idempotent on order ID.

scoreRationale.pain: One detailed, recent request with 28 replies (https://community.shopify.com/t/looking-for-a-solution-for-many-small-unattended-shop-in-shop-locations/686270); no second independent complaint found.
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: Nearest paid apps have 0 reviews (https://apps.shopify.com/placestock) and no freelancer jobs were found for the task.
scoreRationale.reachability: About 20 community searches surfaced one buyer (https://community.shopify.com/t/looking-for-a-solution-for-many-small-unattended-shop-in-shop-locations/686270); App Store is the realistic channel.
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: PlaceStock covers the owner side and Leav covers QR checkout for a few locations (https://apps.shopify.com/swift-mobile-self-checkout).
scoreRationale.feasibility: Stale carts, races on the last unit, duplicate webhooks and shrink are real traps listed in https://community.shopify.com/t/looking-for-a-solution-for-many-small-unattended-shop-in-shop-locations/686270.
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Shopify checkout carries payments; tax by shelf address and host 1099s remain (https://apps.shopify.com/placestock lists partner commissions as a feature).

review.findings: Reviewer rescored 19 to 16 and narrowed the gap to QR-per-shelf checkout plus an off-Shopify stock ledger for unstaffed spots. PlaceStock (2026-08-18, $14.99 to $49.99) already does partner stock and commissions but relies on partners logging sales; Leav Scan & Go does Shopify QR checkout but per Shopify location ($495 unlimited). The original requester is small (under $150/month sales per spot, Plus unaffordable) and said on 2026-10-12 he was in talks with a provider. No second 2026 complaint and no freelancer jobs found.

missing: only 1 on-task complaint; the second evidence item is adjacent
gateGap.closedBy: The validationTest: 3 more brands running the prototype on 5+ shelves would give independent complaints (pain 4), and 2 agreeing to pay $19/month would lift willingnessToPay to 3.

ideas.title: Grab-and-Go Allergen Labels
ideas.summary: For independent New York delis, bakeries, cafés and food trucks that pack food on site: keep each recipe's allergens in one place and print a dated 'Contains' label on a cheap thermal printer, ready for the state's allergen-notice law that starts 2026-11-12.

public.summary: Keeps track of which allergens are in each thing you make and prints the label for it in seconds.
public.problem: From November 12, anything you wrap and put in the case in New York needs a note saying which major allergens it contains. You know your recipes, but swap a supplier's bread or add a pesto and the handwritten sticker is wrong without anyone noticing.
public.forWhom: Owners of small delis, bakeries, cafés, ice cream shops and food trucks that sell food packed on site.
benefits: Print an allergen and date label for any item in seconds
Change a recipe once and every label updates
A shelf chart of allergens for staff and customers
A record of what each label said and when

ideas.problemStatement: New York's law requires a written notice of the nine major allergens on food prepared and packed on the same premises, from 2026-11-12, with no size threshold. Small shops label by hand, and a recipe or supplier change silently makes the label wrong.
ideas.description: The owner enters each recipe once by picking ingredients and sub-recipes, recording each supplier product's 'Contains' statement. The app derives which of the nine major allergens each item contains, asks the owner to confirm, and prints a label with item name, 'Contains:' line and pack date to a Rollo, Munbyn, Brother QL or DYMO printer, or to Avery sheets. Every recipe change is logged with a timestamp, and a one-page allergen chart can be printed for the counter.
ideas.targetCustomer: Owners and managers of independent New York delis, bakeries, sandwich shops, cafés, ice cream parlors and food trucks that sell prepacked items.
ideas.buyer: The owner, on a personal or business card, per location.
ideas.whyNow: The New York law (A6558-A, Chapter 494 of 2025) takes effect 2026-11-12 and reaches every establishment regardless of size; the state issued no guidance, so owners are improvising.
ideas.founderFit: A recipe-to-allergen matrix with label printing is a small, well-bounded web app; accessibility and plain-language labeling are his interests. He has no food-industry network, so the first customers come from walking into shops and from label-printer sellers.

problemEvidence.author: New York State Legislature
problemEvidence.summary: Enacted text: written notice of any major food allergen on food prepared and packed on premises; no other ingredients required; effective one year after signing.

problemEvidence.author: Dana Loof
problemEvidence.summary: Trade vendor post: law effective 2026-11-12, no location-count threshold, manual labeling breaks when recipes change (vendor opinion).

problemEvidence.author: Paige Maseda
problemEvidence.summary: Label seller sells pre-printed allergen stickers for the NY law and suggests handwriting on blanks: owners buy supplies, but the cheap answer is a sticker.

problemEvidence.author: Paul Zuber, Business Council of NYS
problemEvidence.summary: Trade group memo on the predecessor bill: small delis, bakeries and food trucks would need costly labeling software and hardware.

competitors.name: Cakery Bakeries label maker
competitors.gap: Drafts a 'Contains' line from ingredients, but no saved recipes or sub-recipes, no change log, PNG output only, no thermal printing.

competitors.name: BatchBound
competitors.gap: Allergens entered by hand per label; Avery PDF; has a New York template.

competitors.name: ReciPal
competitors.gap: Built for nutrition panels for packaged goods; priced above a corner deli.

competitors.name: DoughOps
competitors.price: Free tier; label printing only on Pro at $99/month
competitors.gap: Bakery operations suite; expensive for labels alone.

competitors.name: TransAct BOHA
competitors.gap: Aimed at multi-location operators.

keyFeatures: Recipe and sub-recipe allergen matrix with supplier 'Contains' statements
Owner confirmation step before any label prints
One-tap printing to common thermal printers and Avery sheets
Timestamped change log of recipes and labels
Printable counter allergen chart

features: Ingredient and recipe entry with the nine allergens
Label template with item, Contains line and pack date
Browser printing to 2x1 inch thermal labels and Avery sheets

ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind, Supabase (auth, Postgres), browser print CSS for label sizes; no LLM at runtime.

pricing.rationale: Must beat the free generator on saved recipes and printing while staying near the cost of stickers; well below ReciPal and DoughOps Pro.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate: 150 New York locations x $9/month = $1,350 MRR, if walk-in and printer-seller channels work; unvalidated.
ideas.distribution: Walk into 20 delis and bakeries in one neighborhood and set it up on their printer; partner with Rollo and Munbyn resellers and bakery suppliers; allergy advocacy groups that backed the bill as a referral channel (unverified).

validationTest.method: Visit 20 New York delis and bakeries in the first two weeks after 2026-11-12, show a working prototype printing on a Rollo, and ask for a $79 annual pre-payment.
validationTest.successCriteria: 5 of 20 pre-pay, or at least 8 say a missing or wrong label was flagged or worried them.
validationTest.cost: Two days in New York, about $300 travel and a $150 printer.

ideas.moat: Low: saved recipe matrices create some lock-in; the free generator could add saving and printing.
compliance: The owner must confirm each allergen derivation; the app never certifies compliance and says it is not legal advice.
Wrong allergen output can cause harm: keep a timestamped audit log and clear disclaimers.
Handle exemptions such as highly refined oils as owner-confirmed notes.
Labels themselves should meet basic legibility (font size, contrast).

risks.risk: A handwritten or pre-printed sticker satisfies the law, so few owners pay.
risks.mitigation: Sell the date label and recipe-change safety, not compliance alone; validate before building more.

risks.risk: The law sets no penalties and no agency guidance, so urgency fades.
risks.mitigation: Watch for the first inspection citations and other states adopting the 2022 Food Code rule.

risks.risk: Liability for a wrong allergen derivation.
risks.mitigation: Owner confirmation on every item and an explicit disclaimer.

scoreRationale.pain: The enacted law asks only for an allergen notice, which a sticker meets (https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/bills/2025/A6558A); the only cost complaint is about an older bill (https://www.bcnys.org/sites/default/files/S.6820%20(Harckham)%20A.7494%20(Lunsford)%20-BCNys.pdf).
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: The supplier answer is pre-printed stickers and handwriting (https://www.onlinelabels.com/articles/what-you-need-to-know-about-new-yorks-allergen-law?src=7); no freelancer jobs found for the task.
scoreRationale.reachability: No owner voices found online; local news quotes only the sponsor (https://www.wxxinews.org/local-news/2025-11-14/new-state-law-requires-food-allergen-labeling-for-deli-and-bakery-products), so reach is door to door.
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: A free tool already drafts the Contains line (https://cakerybakeries.com/labelmaker); the gap is saved recipes, change log and thermal printing.
scoreRationale.feasibility: Simple CRUD plus print CSS; the law needs no ingredient list (https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/bills/2025/A6558A).
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: A wrong derivation can cause anaphylaxis, so liability and disclaimers matter (https://www.transact-tech.com/resources/blog/manual-food-labeling-allergen-compliance notes inspectors will look at labels).

review.findings: Reviewer rescored 18 to 15. The enacted text (A6558-A, Chapter 494) requires only a notice of major allergens, so a handwritten 'Contains' sticker complies; OnlineLabels sells pre-printed allergen stickers for it. The only cost complaint (Business Council, 2023-06-01) targeted a predecessor bill that required full ingredient lists. A free generator (cakerybakeries.com) drafts the Contains line but has no saved recipes, change log or thermal printing; that is the re-scoped gap. No penalties, guidance or delay found. Not killed because no free tool does the saved-recipe, print and audit job.

missing: no complaint dated within 90 days; the only complaint (2023-06-01) concerns a predecessor bill
gateGap.closedBy: The validationTest's door-to-door visits after 2026-11-12: 8 owners describing a flagged or wrong label would be dated complaints (pain 4), and 5 annual pre-payments would lift willingnessToPay to 3.

ideas.title: Fee Disclosure Check for Restaurants
ideas.summary: For independent restaurants in Florida, Colorado and California that add service, kitchen or card charges: upload the menu, website and receipt, and get a line-by-line check of every surcharge against the state's disclosure rules, with suggested wording.

public.summary: Checks your menu, website and receipts for every added charge and shows what your state expects you to say about it.
public.problem: You add a service or kitchen charge to cover rising costs. Then a new state law says it has to be on the menu, in letters as big as your dish descriptions, with the amount and what it pays for. You reprint menus and still are not sure the online ordering page and the receipt match.
public.forWhom: Owners and managers of independent restaurants, cafés and bars that add charges to the bill.
benefits: Find every added charge across menu, website and receipt
See which ones fall short of your state's rules and why
Get plain wording you can put on the menu today
Check again before you reprint, not after

ideas.problemStatement: Florida (from 2026-07-01), Colorado (from 2026-01-01) and California now require restaurants to disclose added charges with the amount and purpose, in specified places and type sizes. Owners are unsure whether a third-party ordering fee counts, what wording works, and whether the online menu and receipt match the printed one.
ideas.description: The owner uploads a menu PDF or photo, pastes the online ordering URL and a sample receipt. The app extracts every surcharge, service charge, auto-gratuity and card fee, measures the disclosure's type size against the menu text, and checks placement, amount and purpose against the cited statute for the chosen state. It produces a findings list with statute references and suggested disclosure wording, and re-checks the online menu when the owner asks. It never certifies compliance.
ideas.targetCustomer: Owners and general managers of independent restaurants, cafés, bars and caterers in Florida, Colorado and California that add charges.
ideas.buyer: The owner, as a one-off purchase per location, often at menu-reprint time.
ideas.whyNow: Florida's SB 606 took effect 2026-07-01 and Colorado's HB25-1090 on 2026-01-01; owners quoted in June 2026 were still unsure what to disclose, and one restaurant spent about $3,000 reprinting menus.
ideas.founderFit: Text extraction, font-size measurement and rule checks are a bounded build he can ship alone; plain-language rewriting of legal requirements suits his writing and teaching background.

problemEvidence.author: Phillip Valys
problemEvidence.summary: Named Florida owners and managers unsure how to disclose charges; Mamush Prime Kosher Grill spent about $3,000 reprinting menus.

problemEvidence.author: Randy Rauch
problemEvidence.summary: Florida law now requires restaurants to disclose service charges before the customer orders.

problemEvidence.author: Tamara Chuang
problemEvidence.summary: Colorado's junk-fee law in force; the Attorney General has received complaints; enforcement under the Consumer Protection Act.

competitors.name: Law-firm checklists (Clark Hill)
competitors.gap: Static checklist; does not read a menu or check type size and placement.

competitors.name: beancount.io compliance guides
competitors.gap: Blog guidance only.

competitors.name: SpotOn junk-fee guide
competitors.gap: Signage advice tied to its POS.

competitors.name: Restaurant lawyers (Greenspoon Marder)
competitors.gap: Advice by appointment; nothing self-serve.

keyFeatures: Surcharge extraction from menu PDF, photo, web page and receipt
Type-size comparison of the disclosure against menu text
Per-state rule checks with statute citations
Suggested disclosure wording to copy
Re-check of the online menu on demand

features: Menu PDF upload with text and font-size extraction

ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind, Supabase, pdf.js for text and font sizes, Tesseract.js for photos, a rules table per state; no paid API on the founder's key at runtime.

pricing.pricePoint: $59 per location, free re-check within 90 days
pricing.rationale: Reviewer found no recurring need once menus are fixed, so a subscription would not hold; well under the $3,000 menu reprint and a lawyer's hour.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate: 300 audits a year x $59 = about $17,700 a year, if menu printers and POS resellers bundle it; unvalidated.
ideas.distribution: Florida menu printers and POS resellers bundling the audit with reprints; Florida Restaurant & Lodging Association chapter newsletters; a free 'paste your menu' type-size checker as a lead magnet.

validationTest.method: Publish a free single-page type-size checker for Florida menus and offer the full audit at $59; contact 3 Florida menu printers about bundling.
validationTest.successCriteria: 15 paid audits in 60 days, or one printer agreeing to resell.

ideas.moat: Low: rule tables per state and printer partnerships; law firms could publish a similar tool.
compliance: Unauthorized practice of law risk: present findings as checks against published statute text, never certify compliance, and offer a lawyer referral.
California exposure is high (class actions under consumer law), so keep California out of the MVP.
Uploaded menus and receipts are low-sensitivity, but receipts may carry card digits: strip them.

risks.risk: One-time need: once menus are fixed, nothing recurs.
risks.mitigation: Price as a one-off audit and sell at reprint time through printers.

risks.risk: Soft enforcement in Florida (no private right of action, small fines) lowers urgency.
risks.mitigation: Track first enforcement actions and add states as laws pass.

risks.risk: Owners read the output as legal advice.
risks.mitigation: Clear framing, statute citations and a lawyer referral.

scoreRationale.pain: Owners are confused and one spent about $3,000 reprinting (https://cbs12.com/features/the-wellness-experience/photos/new-state-law-cracks-down-on-hidden-dining-surcharges-florida-restaurant-fees-service-charges-gratuity-mamush-prime-kosher-grill-boca-raton-dining-town-center-mall-operations-charge-law-florida-law-2026-surcharge-transparency-hidden-restaurant), but that cost is sunk and no penalties have been seen.
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: No paid service or freelancer job for this task found; lawyers publish no flat fee (https://www.gmlaw.com/news/tips-on-tips-floridas-new-law-on-food-service-charges-effective-july-1-2026/).
scoreRationale.reachability: Independent restaurants are hard to reach cold and associations already advise members (https://coloradosun.com/2026/01/17/junk-fees-colorado-consumer-protection-tickets-rents-prices/).
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: Free checklists exist but none reads a menu or checks type size (https://www.clarkhill.com/news-events/news/what-is-colorados-junk-fee-ban-compliance-checklist-for-hotels-restaurants-hospitality-businesses-hb-25-1090/).
scoreRationale.feasibility: PDF text and font-size extraction is routine; the Florida rule is specific about type size and placement (https://mynews13.com/fl/orlando/news/2026/07/03/florida-law-now-requires-restaurants-to-disclose-service-charges-before-customer-s-order).
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Unauthorized-practice-of-law risk and California class-action exposure (https://www.californiaemploymentlawreport.com/2026/04/fridays-five-mandatory-fees-and-service-charges-in-california-what-employers-should-know/).

review.findings: Reviewer rescored 18 to 15 and re-scoped from a $15/month subscription to a one-off audit: the need does not recur once menus are fixed. Florida has no private right of action and small DBPR fines; no enforcement action or lawsuit against a small restaurant found in Florida or Colorado. Free law-firm checklists and vendor guides supply wording, but none checks a menu's type size and placement or the online checkout; that is the remaining gap. The '$3,000 Miami owner' in search snippets was in fact Mamush Prime Kosher Grill in Boca Raton (CBS12/Sun Sentinel, 2026-06-27). Unauthorized-practice-of-law risk noted.

missing: no evidence dated within 90 days (newest owner complaint 2026-06-27)
gateGap.closedBy: The validationTest's free checker and $59 audit: 15 paid audits in 60 days would establish willingnessToPay 3 and supply dated owner complaints toward pain 4.

ideas.title: Recurring Invoice Send Check
ideas.summary: For small firms that bill retainers and maintenance plans through Xero repeating invoices: a daily check that every invoice due today was actually created and marked sent, with a same-day alert when one silently was not.

public.summary: Tells you the same day if one of your automatic monthly invoices did not go out.
public.problem: You set up repeating invoices for your regular clients and trust them to go out on time. When one quietly fails, nothing warns you, and you find out weeks later when the money has not arrived. By then you are chasing a client for a bill they never received.
public.forWhom: Small businesses and freelancers who bill regular clients with automatic repeating invoices.
benefits: Know every scheduled invoice actually went out
Hear about a missed one the same day, not a month later
A monthly list of expected versus sent invoices
No more awkward calls about bills clients never got

ideas.problemStatement: Recurring invoices fail silently: a template stops generating, auto-send is off, or the email never leaves, and the owner learns of it only when a retainer payment does not arrive. Xero has said it has no near-term plan to add sent/not-sent notifications, and a self-hosted Invoice Ninja user saw recurring invoices generated but never emailed with nothing in the logs.
ideas.description: A read-only Xero connection lists every repeating-invoice template and its next scheduled date. Each morning the app compares templates due yesterday and today with the invoices that exist and with each invoice's sent status and history event, and emails or texts the owner a short exception list: not created, created but still draft, or created but never marked sent. A monthly ledger shows expected versus sent per client. QuickBooks Online recurring templates (which already flag bounces natively, but not templates that failed to run or have auto-send off) follow as the second connector.
ideas.targetCustomer: Owners, office managers and outside bookkeepers at small Xero businesses (1 to 20 staff) that bill monthly retainers, memberships or maintenance plans through repeating invoices.
ideas.buyer: The business owner on a company card, or a bookkeeper who adds it per client and passes the cost on.
ideas.whyNow: Xero marked the sent/not-sent notification idea 'Not in pipeline' on 2025-09-09, and a fresh 2026-10-23 report shows recurring invoices still failing with no trace; Xero's developer pricing (2025) made per-connection costs explicit, which a narrow paid app can absorb.
ideas.founderFit: A scheduled comparison job over an accounting API with idempotent alerting is a small Supabase build; the hard part, reasoning about schedules and missed runs, is the kind of systems problem Pisan teaches. He has no bookkeeping network, so distribution relies on the Xero App Store and bookkeeper communities.

problemEvidence.author: Skarema
problemEvidence.summary: Recurring invoices are generated but no longer emailed, 'suddenly stopped working', logs untouched; about 4 users report the same, closed by the maintainer on 2026-10-25 as cannot recreate.

problemEvidence.author: Kelly Munro (Xero community manager), responding to a 2013 idea with 33 votes
problemEvidence.summary: Users ask to be told when an invoice was sent or not sent; Xero says it has no plans to change invoice notifications in the near term and suggests sending a copy to self.

competitors.name: QuickBooks Online delivery errors list
competitors.price: included in QuickBooks Online plans (plan price unknown)
competitors.gap: Flags bounced or undelivered invoice emails, but not a recurring template that failed to run or has auto-send off; QuickBooks only.

competitors.name: Xero invoice history
competitors.gap: Records a 'sent' event per invoice but never alerts when an expected repeating invoice is missing or unsent.

competitors.name: FreeAgent email status
competitors.gap: Shows sent, delivered or bounced per invoice inside FreeAgent only (seen in search results, not fetched).

competitors.name: BillerGenie bounced email report
competitors.gap: A receivables tool's bounce report, not a check that scheduled invoices were created (seen in search results, not fetched).

keyFeatures: Read-only Xero connection listing repeating-invoice templates
Daily expected-versus-actual comparison: not created, still draft, never sent
Same-day email or SMS exception alert, deduplicated
Monthly expected-versus-sent ledger per client
Bookkeeper view across several client organisations

features: Daily comparison job for repeating invoices
outOfScope: Bounce detection (not reliably exposed by Xero's API)
Invoice Ninja and other self-hosted tools
mvpScope.buildEstimate: 2 to 3 weeks, plus Xero app certification

ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind, Supabase (Postgres, auth, scheduled edge functions), Xero Accounting API, Resend for alert email; no LLM at runtime.

pricing.rationale: Below the cost of one missed retainer; must cover Xero's per-connection developer charges above the free 5-connection tier.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate: 300 organisations x $9/month = $2,700 MRR, less Xero connection fees; assumes bookkeepers bring most organisations.
ideas.distribution: Xero App Store listing; posts answering missed-invoice threads in Xero Central and productideas.xero.com; offers to 10 Xero-certified bookkeepers to run it free on their client books for a month.

validationTest.method: Interview 10 Xero bookkeepers about missed repeating invoices in the last 12 months, and run a one-page landing site linked from the Xero idea thread.
validationTest.successCriteria: At least 4 of 10 recall a silent missed repeating invoice and 3 agree to a paid pilot at $9 per organisation.

ideas.moat: Weak: the history of expected-versus-sent per client is the only accumulating asset; speed and a bookkeeper-friendly multi-client view are the real edge.
compliance: Xero app certification is required on every tier; the free developer tier allows 5 connections
Financial data: read-only scopes, minimal retention, data processing agreement for UK and EU customers (GDPR)
Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA for the dashboard

risks.mitigation: Xero said on 2025-09-09 it has no near-term plan; keep the product cheap and multi-platform.

risks.risk: Few businesses ever see a silent failure
risks.mitigation: The validation test measures frequency before any build.
Price per organisation above Xero's per-connection cost and sell bookkeeper bundles.

scoreRationale.pain: Real silent failures in Invoice Ninja (https://github.com/invoiceninja/invoiceninja/issues/13385) and a long-running QuickBooks thread (https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/other-questions/reoccurring-invoices-not-sending-emails/00/1420171), but no first-hand loss amounts.
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: No payment evidence: the Xero idea drew 33 votes in a decade (https://productideas.xero.com/forums/967115-invoices-quotes/suggestions/44960542-sales-notification-that-invoice-sent-not-sent); capped at 2.
scoreRationale.reachability: Users gather in vendor idea boards and app stores (https://productideas.xero.com/forums/967115-invoices-quotes/suggestions/44960542-sales-notification-that-invoice-sent-not-sent), but none of them is a confirmed buyer.
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: QuickBooks covers bounces natively (https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/view-list-bounced-emails-delivery-errors/L88qTcb6b) but neither it nor Xero alerts on a template that did not run.
scoreRationale.feasibility: Creation and sent status are readable via the API, but bounce data is likely not; certification adds time (https://developer.xero.com/pricing).
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Xero certification is mandatory and paid tiers start beyond 5 connections (https://developer.xero.com/pricing).

review.findings: Reviewer rescored 19 to 17. Invoice Ninja #13385 is a self-hosted Docker bug closed as cannot-recreate, so it is weak as a market and was dropped as the starting platform. QuickBooks Online already lists bounced and undelivered invoices for free, so the scope narrowed to Xero repeating invoices that were not created or not marked sent, with QuickBooks failed-template checks second. Xero does not notify on failed sends and said so on 2025-09-09. No paid monitor found; app stores not searched. Feasibility and compliance lowered by one each for Xero certification and connection pricing.

gateGap.closedBy: The bookkeeper interviews close the largest gap, willingnessToPay: 3 paid pilots would lift it to 3, and 4 of 10 recalling a silent miss would support pain 4.

ideas.title: Transfer Enquiry Desk
ideas.summary: For owner-operated airport-transfer and chauffeur firms without a WordPress booking plugin: a hosted enquiry link that validates each journey, keeps outbound and return legs linked, and lets the owner confirm from a phone so customers get an honest 'received' or 'confirmed' message.

public.summary: Gives your transfer business one booking link that collects complete journey details and lets you confirm each trip from your phone.
public.problem: Enquiries arrive by WhatsApp, phone and email with missing pickup times, passenger counts or return dates. A return trip gets mixed up with the outbound one, and customers are not sure whether their ride is booked or only requested. You end up chasing details and hoping nobody is left waiting at arrivals.
public.forWhom: Owners of small airport-transfer, chauffeur and minibus firms.
benefits: Every enquiry arrives complete, with nothing to chase
Outbound and return trips kept together but never mixed up
Customers know whether a trip is requested or confirmed
Confirm a booking with one tap from your phone
All trips in one tidy spreadsheet

ideas.problemStatement: A small private airport-transfer business wants new booking enquiries captured with pickup, destination, date, passengers and contact, routed to a sheet and the team, but does not know how to handle missing or invalid fields; replies add that outbound and return trips on the same day get merged and that 'booking' and 'enquiry' are not distinguished.
ideas.description: The owner gets a hosted booking link to put in a Google Business profile, Instagram bio or WhatsApp auto-reply. The form validates pickup and drop-off, flight time, date not in the past, passengers and luggage, and stores outbound and return as two legs under one submission ID. Each request lands as an 'enquiry' and the customer is told so; the owner taps confirm (or decline with a reason) on a phone, which sends the customer the confirmed message and writes the leg to a Google Sheet. No dispatch, payments or driver app.
ideas.targetCustomer: Owner-operators of airport-transfer, chauffeur and minibus firms with 1 to 10 vehicles that take bookings by phone, WhatsApp or email and have no WordPress booking plugin.
ideas.buyer: The owner, on a personal or company card.
ideas.whyNow: Small operators now try to build this themselves in Make (2026-10-02), while the existing tools are WordPress plugins (E-cab, updated 2026-10-27) or dispatch suites priced in thousands.
ideas.founderFit: A validated form, a two-leg data model, an SMS or email notification and a Sheets sync is a weekend Supabase build. He has no transport network, so first customers come from automation forums and local operator directories.

problemEvidence.author: Cambridge_Transfers
problemEvidence.summary: Private airport-transfer owner asks how to capture and validate booking enquiries and route them to a sheet and the team; replies raise same-day return-leg merging and booking-versus-enquiry status.

problemEvidence.author: MagePeople
problemEvidence.summary: E-cab taxi and chauffeur booking plugin: 2,000 active installs, 28 ratings, with a paid Pro version ($69/year or $99 lifetime on the vendor page).

competitors.name: E-cab Taxi Booking Manager (free and Pro)
competitors.price: Free; Pro $69/year per domain or $99 lifetime
competitors.gap: Needs WordPress and WooCommerce; no visible enquiry-versus-confirmed status or Sheets export.

competitors.name: Chauffeur Booking System
competitors.gap: Strong feature set including return trips and alerts, but it is a self-installed WordPress plugin.

competitors.name: Cab Grid
competitors.gap: Fare grid with 'please call to book' in the free version; booking form and returns are Pro only, on WordPress.

competitors.name: Onde
competitors.gap: Full dispatch platform for larger fleets.

keyFeatures: Hosted booking link, no website needed
Journey validation: date, flight time, passengers, luggage
Outbound and return legs linked by one submission ID
Enquiry versus confirmed status with honest customer messages
One-tap confirm from the owner's phone and Google Sheets sync
ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind, Supabase (Postgres, auth, edge functions), Google Sheets API, email via Resend and optional SMS via the owner's Twilio account; no LLM at runtime.

pricing.rationale: The reviewer found one-time WordPress plugins at $69 to $99, so a hosted tool must stay near $100 a year to compete.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate: 150 operators x $9/month = $1,350 MRR; assumes operators without WordPress sites find it through forums and Google Business profiles.
ideas.distribution: Answer transfer and chauffeur booking threads in Make and n8n communities; contact 30 small operators listed on Google Maps near three UK and US airports with a free first month.

validationTest.method: Build a clickable demo link and message 30 small transfer operators found on Google Maps, offering a free month in exchange for a 15-minute call.
validationTest.successCriteria: At least 8 replies, 5 calls, and 3 operators who say they handle enquiries by WhatsApp or phone and agree to pay $9 a month after the trial.

ideas.moat: Weak: a simple form product. The edge is being hosted and WordPress-free, with operator-specific details (flights, returns, luggage) built in.
compliance: GDPR and UK GDPR: passenger names, phone numbers and trip details; data processing agreement and a retention limit
No payments, so no PCI scope
Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA for the public booking form

risks.risk: Operators already use free Google Forms or a $99 plugin
risks.mitigation: Target operators without websites; validation test checks this first.
The outreach test measures demand before building.
Keep support minimal and the product self-serve.

scoreRationale.pain: One pre-launch design question from a single owner (https://community.make.com/t/116396); no other operator complaint found.
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: Operators pay, but one-time: E-cab Pro $69/year or $99 lifetime (https://mage-people.com/product/wordpress-taxi-cab-booking-plugin-for-woocommerce/) and Chauffeur Booking System $99 (https://codecanyon.net/item/chauffeur-booking-system-for-wordpress/21072773).
scoreRationale.reachability: Owners are scattered; only one surfaced in automation forums (https://community.make.com/t/116396).
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: Chauffeur Booking System already has return trips, statuses and alerts on WordPress (https://codecanyon.net/item/chauffeur-booking-system-for-wordpress/21072773).
scoreRationale.feasibility: A form, a status flag, Sheets sync and notifications, as the Make thread outlines (https://community.make.com/t/116396).
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Passenger contact data needs GDPR care but no payments are taken (https://wordpress.org/plugins/ecab-taxi-booking-manager/).

review.findings: Reviewer rescored 18 to 16: pain 3 to 2 (one thread, a design question, return-leg and status points came from repliers) and willingnessToPay 3 to 2 (comparable WordPress tools sell for $69 to $99 one-time). Not killed: no free product found does the hosted, WordPress-free enquiry-versus-confirmed flow with linked legs and Sheets sync. Re-scoped to operators without WordPress who book by phone or WhatsApp, at about $9/month.

gateGap.closedBy: The operator outreach test closes the largest gaps: 3 operators committing to $9/month would lift willingnessToPay to 3, and 5 calls describing lost or garbled enquiries would support pain 4.

ideas.title: Mixed-Use Vehicle Worksheet
ideas.summary: For sole proprietors who use one vehicle for both a Schedule C business and Schedule E rentals: upload a mileage export and get the combined qualified business-use percentage, the per-schedule split, a prior-year recapture check and the statement to attach.

public.summary: Turns your mileage log into the vehicle numbers you need when one car or truck serves both your business and your rental properties.
public.problem: You drive the same vehicle for your business and for your rentals, and your tax software treats them as two separate assets. Split that way, neither use looks big enough to qualify, even though together they clearly do. You are left guessing how to enter it and how to explain it if asked.
public.forWhom: Self-employed people and small landlords who use one vehicle for both a business and rental properties.
benefits: See your combined business-use share in minutes
Know how to split vehicle costs between business and rentals
Get a ready-to-attach explanation
Spot when a drop in business use could cost you

ideas.problemStatement: A filer using one truck for a Schedule C business and Schedule E rentals finds that splitting it into two assets in tax software makes each fail the more-than-50% qualified business use test (40% and 20%), although combined use is 60%; the accepted answer says to test per asset on one Form 4562 and prorate across schedules, and notes TurboTax may not support it easily.
ideas.description: The user uploads a CSV from any mileage tracker and tags trips as business, rental or personal (rules can auto-tag by destination). The worksheet computes combined qualified business use per vehicle, the more-than-50% test, standard-mileage versus actual-expense figures split by schedule, and a recapture warning when use falls to 50% or below compared with prior years. It produces a PDF statement and step-by-step entry notes for common tax software. It is a calculator with citations, not tax advice.
ideas.targetCustomer: Sole proprietors and side-business owners who also own one to five rental properties and share a vehicle between them.
ideas.buyer: The filer, on a personal card, once per tax year.
ideas.whyNow: A 2026-10-14 question shows mainstream software still tests each split asset separately, and landlord mileage apps such as LandMile (launched 2026) log trips but do not compute the combined test.
ideas.founderFit: Pure arithmetic over a CSV with clear rules is a weekend React build with no server-side data. He has no tax network, so it depends on search traffic and landlord communities, and the tax-liability framing needs care.

problemEvidence.author: user4910112
problemEvidence.summary: Shared truck used 40% for Schedule C and 20% for Schedule E fails the 50% test when split into two assets; accepted answer: test per asset on one Form 4562 and prorate, TurboTax may not support it easily.

competitors.name: LandMile
competitors.gap: Logs and tags landlord trips with CSV export; no combined business-use test or per-schedule allocation.

competitors.name: Everlance
competitors.price: $0 Basic; paid tiers listed at conflicting prices on the page
competitors.gap: General mileage tracking; no combined qualified-use test found.

competitors.name: TurboTax vehicle worksheets
competitors.gap: Tests the 50% rule per split asset, which is the failure the question describes.

keyFeatures: CSV import from any mileage tracker
Trip tagging by schedule with destination rules
Combined qualified-use percentage and the more-than-50% test
Per-schedule standard versus actual expense split
Prior-year recapture warning and a PDF statement to attach
ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind, all computation in the browser, PDF generation client-side; Supabase only for license keys; no LLM at runtime.

pricing.rationale: A once-a-year calculation; below LandMile's $39.99 annual price for logging.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate: 500 filers x $19 = $9,500 per tax season; assumes search traffic from tax-season questions.
ideas.distribution: Answers on money.stackexchange.com and TurboTax community threads about shared vehicles; a free calculator page that ranks for the question, with the PDF statement as the paid step; landlord forums.

validationTest.method: Publish a free one-page calculator during January to March and put the PDF statement behind a $19 payment.
validationTest.successCriteria: 300 calculator uses and at least 15 paid statements in the season.
validationTest.cost: One weekend and about $20 for a domain.

ideas.moat: Weak: simple math. The edge is a precise, cited treatment of an awkward case, plus search ranking.
compliance: Tax liability: practitioners disagree on the treatment; present as a calculator with cited rules and a clear not-tax-advice notice
Privacy: all computation in the browser, no trip data stored
Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA

risks.risk: The case is too narrow to sustain revenue
risks.mitigation: Ship as a cheap seasonal calculator, not a subscription.

risks.risk: Wrong treatment exposes users to recapture
risks.mitigation: Show both readings practitioners use, with citations, and a prior-year recapture check.

risks.risk: Tax software fixes the entry path
risks.mitigation: Keep the build to a weekend so the downside is small.

scoreRationale.pain: Happens once per vehicle per year and one good answer resolved it (https://money.stackexchange.com/questions/170088).
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: Filers already pay for logging, e.g. LandMile $39.99/year (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/property-miles/id6760436282); no one pays for the calculation itself.
scoreRationale.reachability: The Schedule C plus E shared-vehicle combination is narrow; search traffic is the channel (https://money.stackexchange.com/questions/170088).
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: Trackers stop at logging and tax software tests split assets separately (https://ttlc.intuit.com/community/investments-and-rental-properties/discussion/re-hi-i-use-my-car-for-business-purpose-i-m-a-part-time-real-estate-agent-and-also-for-my-per/01/3546723).
scoreRationale.feasibility: Simple arithmetic over a CSV export that trackers already provide (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/property-miles/id6760436282).
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Practitioners disagree and recapture risk applies when use drops to 50% or below (https://ttlc.intuit.com/community/tax-credits-deductions/discussion/bonus-depreciation-on-vehicle/00/1723767/amp).

review.findings: Reviewer rescored 16 to 15. The question is a single TurboTax entry problem, solved by an accepted answer, and the asker's Schedule C business rents the truck on Turo, so the case is narrow and once a year. Logging is already served (LandMile $39.99/year, Everlance free Basic), so the idea was re-scoped from a tracker to a one-vehicle Form 4562 worksheet sold per tax year. Compliance lowered to 2 because the treatment is disputed and carries recapture risk.

gateGap.closedBy: The seasonal paid-statement test closes the largest gap, willingnessToPay: 15 paid statements would lift it to 3 and supply the second evidence item.

runNotes.caveats: Three provisional ideas ship (16, 15, 15); none came near the gate of 22. Seven candidates were researched and adversarially reviewed: two were killed (Payout Explainer: Payout Match and PayoutCheck already do it; Venue Update Page: the Facebook cap limits links only and Buffer's free plan covers the job), one was rescored but failed the 180-day floor (food truck broadcaster), one was rescored to 14 (Crew Log by WhatsApp) and not shipped because three ideas already qualified, and three survived as provisional after rescoring. As on 2026-11-05, community.shopify.com back-office and booking threads are dominated by developers promoting their own apps, and every booking niche checked (classes, rentals, salons) already has several paid apps; the strongest fresh signals today were mandates (New York allergen notices from 2026-11-12, Florida and Colorado fee disclosure) whose cheapest compliance path is a sticker or a reprint, which caps willingness to pay. No idea is validated, so no candidate has willingnessToPay 3 or more. Two of the three ideas share the category Accessibility & Compliance (the maximum). All three have small-business buyers.
